GUIYANG · CHENGDU · MARCH 2027

Cherry blossom in Guizhou, then pandas and teahouses in Chengdu.

Three nights in Guiyang buy two shots at the Pingba cherry blossom, Tuesday as the main attempt and Wednesday held in reserve, with Qingyan Ancient Town as the fallback. Then the G train to Chengdu for four nights of pandas, teahouses and day trips, and a morning flight home. Watch the garden’s live stream from early March before you commit the day.

Tue Mar 23Blossom
The blossom day — Gui’an / Pingba, all of it.
  • Gui’an (Pingba) Cherry Blossom Garden — around 700,000 trees across 24,000 mu, Guinness-certified as the largest cherry blossom base in the world. Entry is free; only the shuttle costs anything, about ¥15 one way or ¥30 return
  • About an hour from Guiyang by car. Be inside the gate by 07:00. The two good windows are 07:00–11:00 and after 17:00 — soft light, thinner crowds, and the midday hours are the worst of both
  • Tuesday is deliberately the earlier of your two days. Every recent season has run mid-March, so the risk here is being late, not early — and going first leaves Wednesday as a second attempt
  • It is a weekday. This is a free, nationally famous site an hour from a provincial capital; peak-bloom weekends are genuinely punishing
  • Ask staff which zone is best today. The garden runs across hills — higher and north-facing slopes lag the sunny lower ground by days, so there is usually colour somewhere even when the flagship avenues have turned
  • Three named areas: Fanying Square, Xunying Garden, Manying Garden. Walk or take the shuttle between them
Wed Mar 24Reserve
Second blossom run — or Qingyan, if yesterday delivered.
  • Decide this over breakfast, based on what you actually saw yesterday. This is the day the third Guiyang night bought you, and it exists to de-risk the blossom
  • If Tuesday was thin or early — go back. A second run costs you nothing but the drive, and 24 hours can visibly change the garden mid-season
  • If Tuesday delivered — Qingyan Ancient Town, 29 km out, about 27 minutes by car or a ¥10 bus from Guiyang Railway Station. A walled Ming–Qing stone town with real gates and flagstones, not a rebuild. Eat along the main lane: rose sugar cake, braised pig’s trotters, tofu balls
  • If the weather turned — Huangla Village is the sheltered option: smaller, far less crowded, higher viewpoint, and it held blossom better than Pingba through the 2025 cold snap
  • Whatever you do, be back for a proper sour soup fish dinner. It is the dish Guizhou is actually about, and tomorrow you leave
Thu Mar 25Travel
Breakfast, then three hours north — lunch in Chengdu.
  • After breakfast, Guiyang North → Chengdu East, ~3 hours on a G train. 84 pairs a day, so a mid-morning departure is easy
  • Arrive early afternoon and drop bags
  • Gentle first afternoon: People’s Park and the Heming teahouse — bamboo chairs, refillable tea, ear-cleaners, dancing
  • Evening: Jinli or Taikoo Li, or a Chengdu hotpot — noticeably milder than the Chongqing version

Blossom timing — read this one

  • THREE-YEAR RECORD2024: forecast peak Mar 15–23 — but live updates showed only ~40% open on Mar 20 and advised coming after the 25th. 2025: meteorological bureau gave Mar 17–25. 2026: bloom from early March, garden fully open Mar 7, and reporters found large-scale petal fall by Mar 17. The mass bloom runs mid-March, not late March.
  • THE SOURCES DISAGREE, AND BOTH ARE RIGHTNews reports and met-bureau forecasts track the hua hai — the white early cherry opening all at once. That spectacle is short: about ten days, mid-March. Travel guides give a much wider window because they track whether there is any blossom: early cherry late Feb–late March, late cherry mid-March–mid-April. Different questions, different answers.
  • WHAT TUESDAY THE 23RD ACTUALLY GETS YOULate for the white, comfortably inside the pink. In a 2025-style late season the early cherry is still going; in a 2026-style early season it has gone but the deep-pink late cherry is opening. Since either colour was fine, that is a workable position — what you cannot reach, without moving the wedding, is the white mass-bloom postcard.
  • WHY TUESDAY AND NOT WEDNESDAYEvery recent season has run earlier than late March, so the risk is arriving after the peak, not before it. Going Tuesday moves you toward the bloom and still leaves Wednesday as a genuine second attempt — the thing the third Guiyang night was spent on.
  • THE REAL RISK IS COLLAPSE, NOT LATENESSIn March 2025 a sudden cold, rainy spell cut the Pingba bloom from its usual ~10 days to about five. The window does not just move — it can shorten once open. That is the argument for two attempts rather than one perfectly-chosen day.
  • CHECK THE LIVESTREAM FIRSTGuiyang Broadcasting runs a 24-hour multi-camera slow livestream of the garden through the season — it opened on 4 March in 2026. From early March 2027 you can see the exact bloom state before committing the day. This is worth more than any forecast in this card.

Eat — Guizhou

  • THE ONESour soup fish (suan tang yu) — the defining Guizhou dish, and genuinely different from Sichuan: a fermented tomato and rice-water broth that is sour first, spicy second. Book a proper sit-down one evening.
  • BREAKFASTBeef noodles (niu rou fen) — rice noodles in clear or red broth, the standard morning meal. Best before 09:00, and the reason to skip the hotel buffet.
  • ORDER THISSiwawa, literally “silk dolls” — shredded vegetables in a thin pancake you roll yourself and dip in sour chilli water.
  • STREETGrilled tofu and lao guo around Erqi Road after dark. At Qingyan, the local things are rose sugar cake and braised trotters.
  • TAKE HOMELaoganma chilli oil is from Guizhou. Cheaper here, and there are varieties that never leave the province.

Worth Knowing

On the photos: Pingba’s own planting is not on Wikimedia Commons, so the blossom image at the top of this document is a cherry tree elsewhere in China, shown for the look of it rather than the place. Everything else here is Guizhou.

Guiyang sits at about 1,100 m, so evenings run colder than Chengdu or Chongqing despite similar daytime highs. It is also the wettest of the three stops — roughly 15 rain days in March — and it is where you most need to be outdoors. A real shell, not a windbreaker.

Three nights, arriving Monday lunchtime — so your full days are Tuesday and Wednesday. The blossom takes Tuesday, and Wednesday is a genuine second attempt rather than a wasted spare. That is the whole reason Guiyang was given its maximum.

Cut Guiyang to two nights and there is no second attempt at all — you would be betting the entire blossom on one morning, in a place whose bloom window has moved by more than a week across the last three years.

Huangguoshu Waterfall is deliberately out. It is a long day each way, and March is its thinnest flow of the year — it runs at full volume in July and August. Spending a day there would cost you the blossom insurance and show you the waterfall at its worst.

Fri Mar 26Day trip
Leshan Giant Buddha — on your only weekday, on purpose.
  • High-speed train Chengdu → Leshan, ~1 hour, about ¥41–55 in second class, then a short bus or taxi to the park
  • The 71-metre Buddha deserves 2–3 hours. The point is the stairway cut down the cliff beside it — and that stair is the worst queue on this trip, routinely two hours at weekends. Go straight to it on arrival and loop the temples afterwards
  • This is why Leshan goes first. Friday is the only weekday you have in Chengdu, and it belongs to the site that punishes weekends hardest
  • The boat option shows you the whole Buddha head-on in about 30 minutes with no stairs at all — worth doing as well as the walk, not instead of
  • Back in Chengdu for dinner; about 8 hours door to door
Sat Mar 27Nature
Pandas at opening, then bronze masks up the road.
  • Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding — be at the gate for opening (~07:30). The most time-sensitive thing in Chengdu: pandas feed and move 08:00–10:00, then sleep through the middle of the day. Arriving early beats the weekend crowd as well as the nap
  • Afternoon: Sanxingdui Museum in Guanghan — both sites are north of the city, so they pair naturally. 18 minutes by rail from Chengdu North (~¥8), entry ~¥72
  • Three-thousand-year-old bronze masks and figures from a civilisation nobody knew existed until 1986. Entirely indoors, and the strongest thing in Chengdu regardless of weather
  • Book Sanxingdui online in advance. It has been one of the busiest museums in China since the 2021 finds, and a Saturday slot is exactly the one that sells out
  • Chengdu has its own cherry blossom in late March — ask at the hotel what is out. City parks usually have something, and it is a free second bite after Guizhou
Sun Mar 28Options
Mountain or a slow city day — your last one.
  • Decide this on how tired you are. Three consecutive days out of the city is a lot, and Chengdu is the one place on this trip that rewards doing nothing
  • If you have the legs — Mount Qingcheng & Dujiangyan. Intercity train ~30–40 min from Chengdu Xibu (a third station — check your ticket). Taoist temples and forest paths, alongside irrigation works from 256 BC that still function. March supplies mist and the mountain suits it
  • If you do not — stay put. Wuhou Shrine and Jinli next door, Jinsha Site Museum if Sanxingdui left you wanting more, and an afternoon in a teahouse. That is a legitimate use of a Chengdu Sunday
  • Evening: Sichuan opera at Shufeng Yayun — face-changing, fire-breathing, hand shadows. Touristy and worth it. Book a day ahead
  • Pack tonight. Tomorrow is an early start
Mon Mar 29Travel
Early start, then home by mid-afternoon.
  • SQ 847 is booked — departs Chengdu Tianfu 10:00, lands Singapore 15:10. Boeing 787-10, 5h10, CNY 1,350 per adult in Economy
  • TFU is about 50 km out. For a 10:00 departure you want to be at the airport by 08:00, which means leaving the city around 07:00. Arrange the car the night before — do not gamble on a morning Didi
  • Today is not a sightseeing day. That is the trade for landing home at 15:10 with the evening still yours rather than arriving near midnight
  • The upside: Sunday stays a genuine full last day instead of a half one

Worth Knowing

Four nights, and only one weekday among them. You arrive Thursday lunchtime, and Friday is the single Mon–Fri day you get. It goes to Leshan, because the cliff stairway is the one queue here that genuinely doubles at weekends.

Saturday works because pandas are an early-morning activity anyway. You are through the gate at 07:30 and out by 10:30, ahead of the crowd, with the afternoon for Sanxingdui — book that slot online in advance.

Sunday is deliberately optional. Qingcheng if you have the legs, a teahouse if you do not. After Chongqing stairs, a Guizhou blossom dawn and a Leshan day trip, having one day you are allowed to waste is not laziness — it is the reason the trip still feels like a holiday at the end.

Ending here is right. Chengdu is the softest of the three cities — flat, excellent metro, famously slow — which is what you want at the end of a trip rather than the start.

Eat — Chengdu

  • THE ONEHotpot — the mala original, numbing Sichuan pepper as much as chilli. Ask for wei la (mild) or a divided pot. Yulin is where locals eat it; Kuanzhai is the convenient version.
  • CHEAP, EVERYWHEREThe snack trio — dan dan noodles, sweet water noodles, Zhong dumplings. A few yuan each, and better from a hole in the wall than a restaurant.
  • DO IT ONCEChuan chuan xiang — skewers cooked in hotpot broth, priced by the stick. The low-commitment way into hotpot flavours.
  • CLASSICMapo tofu — Chen Mapo Tofu is the original house, still good if touristy.
  • DRINKTea, not coffee. An afternoon of refills in a park teahouse is the local pastime and costs almost nothing.

Rainy-day swaps

  • ALREADY BOOKED INSanxingdui sits on Saturday afternoon regardless — it is the strongest thing in Chengdu and entirely indoors, so it needs no weather at all.
  • IF FRIDAY IS WETLeshan still works — but skip the cliff stairway, which gets slick and slow, and take the boat instead. You see the whole Buddha head-on in 30 minutes.
  • IF SUNDAY IS FOULDrop Qingcheng and take the city option. Jinsha Site Museum is the indoor replacement — same Shu civilisation as Sanxingdui, no train needed.
  • COVEREDHeming teahouse in People’s Park — a covered pavilion; rain arguably improves it. The correct destination for a genuinely bad afternoon.

On accuracy: flight times and aircraft are from current published schedules and should be reconfirmed at booking, since airlines routinely re-time seasonally. Train durations are typical G-train times, not specific services. The cherry blossom dates are the one genuinely uncertain thing here — Pingba ran Mar 15–23 in 2024, Mar 17–25 in 2025, and was already dropping petals by Mar 17 in 2026, so the mass bloom is a mid-March event and Tuesday the 23rd is aimed at the late-cherry tail rather than the peak. Treat this document as correctly aimed rather than confirmed and recheck in February 2027. Weather figures are 30-year normals, not a forecast. Ticket prices in yuan are indicative.
